title: Aalborg University Orders ConScience Plug'N'Teach Superconducting Quantum Computer for Hands-On Engineering Training - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Aalborg University has ordered an on-premises ConScience Plug’N’Teach superconducting quantum computer (2 qubits expanding to 7, installed 2027) built with Quantum Machines control electronics and Bluefors cryogenics, for hands-on engineering training. It marks bootstrapped Swedish supplier ConScience's move from standalone chips into integrated educational systems aimed at the quantum hardware workforce bottleneck.

insights.claim: Aalborg University will install a ConScience Plug’N’Teach superconducting quantum computer in 2027 that launches with two qubits and later expands to seven qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Small-qubit teaching systems are emerging as a distinct, non-performance-driven hardware market segment.

insights.claim: Aalborg University is choosing on-premises cryogenic hardware over cloud-based simulation or remote processor access so engineering students can train directly on cryogenic operation, microwave control, and qubit readout.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Universities may become a steady buyer base for physical small quantum systems, not just cloud access customers.

insights.claim: The ConScience Plug’N’Teach full-stack platform integrates ConScience superconducting processors with Quantum Machines control and readout electronics and Bluefors dilution refrigeration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum Machines and Bluefors capture value across even small educational deployments, reinforcing their picks-and-shovels position.

insights.claim: Gothenburg-based ConScience AB, operating from Chalmers University of Technology cleanrooms, has grown organically without external venture capital by selling superconducting qubit devices such as its Qubit-in-a-box line to academic labs and commercial developers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A rare revenue-funded quantum hardware vendor; a possible acquisition or funding target as it scales into systems.
